basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 10.' and it opens 'Vers. 10. Igitur egressus Jacob de Bersabee. Jacob, ut diximus, Christum significat, qui,'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 10. Igitur egressus Jacob de Bersabee. Jacob, ut diximus, Christum significat, qui, relictis parentibus, id est Judaeis, de quibus carnem assumpserat, relicta etiam domo, id est Hierusalem, patria quoque, id est Judaea, relicta, perrexit ad gentes, ubi Ecclesiam sponsam acciperet.
